meta.scalability_note: 2 German regions (Frankfurt/Main, Berlin); enterprise-grade auto-scaling; up to 120 vCPUs; primarily EU/German footprint; no global CDN
meta.performance_note: Enterprise-grade SLA backed by Schwarz Group infrastructure; ISO 27001 certified datacenters; strong uptime guarantees for business-critical workloads; GDPR-compliant by design

AWS Amplify.note: No managed web/mobile app hosting platform. Apps are deployed on VMs or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: Serverless Functions available in beta. Limited runtime support and throughput vs AWS Lambda.

Amazon ECS.note: Container workloads fully supported via Kubernetes. Docker-based deployments work natively on SKE.

Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes with automated upgrades, monitoring integration, and private networking.

Amazon EC2.note: On-demand and reserved VMs in Frankfurt and Berlin. GPU instances available for AI workloads.

AWS Batch.note: Batch workloads supported via VMs and Kubernetes Jobs. No dedicated managed batch service.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage with standard S3 API. Available in both German regions. High durability.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: Cold storage tier available in Object Storage. Less feature-rich than AWS Glacier Flexible/Deep Archive.

Amazon EBS.note: Persistent block volumes attachable to Cloud Servers. SSD-backed with high IOPS.

AWS Backup.note: Managed backup service for VMs and volumes with scheduled policies and retention management.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed elastic NFS-compatible file system.

Amazon RDS.note: Fully managed PostgreSQL and MySQL with automated backups, high availability, and monitoring.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed serverless NoSQL key-value database.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: Fully managed Redis with clustering, replication, and TLS. Production-ready managed caching.

Amazon Redshift.note: Managed OpenSearch for search and log analytics. No columnar data warehouse comparable to Redshift.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with TLS termination, health checks, and path routing.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP/UDP load balancing supported in the same managed product. High-throughput capable.

Amazon VPC.note: Isolated private networks with custom subnets, routing, and security groups. Full VPC equivalent.

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS with zone management, record types, and TTL control. No advanced routing policies.

Amazon API Gateway.note: Basic API management capabilities. Full managed API gateway not yet a standalone product.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No native CDN service. Third-party CDNs must be used.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Private dedicated connectivity available leveraging Schwarz Group's enterprise backbone network.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image recognition API.

Amazon SageMaker.note: GPU-enabled VMs and managed JupyterHub for ML workloads. No end-to-end MLOps pipeline or AutoML.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed GenAI / foundation model API service.

AWS Glue.note: No managed serverless ETL / data pipeline service.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data cluster service (Spark/Hadoop).

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless SQL analytics over object storage.

AWS IAM.note: RBAC-based IAM with users, groups, service accounts, and resource-level permissions.

Amazon Cognito.note: No dedicated app-level user authentication. IAM covers platform-level access management only.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: SAML-based SSO via Schwarz Group corporate identity. Limited to console and API access.

AWS KMS.note: Managed encryption key lifecycle management integrated with storage and compute services.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: Managed secrets storage with API access for applications. Supports rotation and versioning.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: Managed TLS certificate provisioning and auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt and private CA.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: Basic security event monitoring and alerting. No ML-based threat detection comparable to GuardDuty.

AWS Security Hub.note: BSI C5 and ISO 27001 compliance posture visible in portal. No unified findings aggregation service.

AWS Config.note: Resource change tracking available through audit logs. No rule-based compliance enforcement service.

AWS Shield.note: Network-level DDoS protection included across all services. Backed by Schwarz Group enterprise network.

AWS WAF.note: Managed WAF with OWASP rule sets available for workloads exposed via Load Balancer.

AWS CloudTrail.note: Comprehensive API audit trail for all STACKIT services. Meets BSI C5 and GDPR audit requirements.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Managed Prometheus and Grafana for metrics and dashboards. Log management available separately. Less unified than CloudWatch.

Amazon SNS.note: Alert notifications via email and webhooks available through the Observability stack. No managed pub/sub service.

AWS Systems Manager.note: VM management, patching, and SSH access tools available. No unified SSM-equivalent with parameter store.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed cost tracking and reporting per project and service in the STACKIT portal.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI/CD build service. External CI/CD tools (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions) are used.

Amazon ECR.note: Managed OCI/Docker container registry with vulnerability scanning.

AWS CloudFormation.note: Official STACKIT Terraform provider for IaC. No native CloudFormation-equivalent.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT MQTT broker or device connectivity service.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device registry or fleet management.

Amazon SQS.note: Managed RabbitMQ-based message queuing. AMQP and MQTT protocols supported.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or serverless event routing service.

Amazon SES.note: Transactional email available via Schwarz Group partnerships. Not a standalone managed SES-equivalent.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time streaming data service.
